discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 271813
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
113 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Occasional light rain is expected to continue and then
  diminish from west to east into early tonight. 

- Another round of rain late Saturday night into Sunday night
  followed by blustery/windy conditions behind a cold front for 
  Sunday night into Monday.

- The coldest conditions are expected Monday and Monday night 
  followed by a warming trend. The next chance of rain will be 
  late in the work week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 109 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

An expansive cutoff low was climbing northeastward toward the 
Northeast today as another trough was moving eastward from the 
Western US. Warming is expected to take place this afternoon as the 
main area of vorticity surrounding the upper low departs the area 
meaning the mix of snow (with times of drizzle because of DGZ 
saturation) with rain should just become rain this afternoon. At the 
base of this approaching mid level trough, a moderate shortwave was 
moving east-northeastward toward the area, but subsidence behind the 
departing upper low should keep the area mostly dry overnight. There 
is some indication in the RRFS, the ECMWF, and to some extent, the 
HRRR that some weak areas of weak precip may attempt to occur 
Saturday morning mainly north of US-6, but it'll need to overcome 
some low level dry air. Temps appear fairly marginal for snow so 
will lean rain at this juncture. Otherwise, the bulk of the area 
leans dry Saturday. There could be some 20 mph wind gusts to finish 
out the day Saturday as the upper low departs the area and weak 
mixing ensues. Another vort max rounds the base of the trough 
Saturday through the Southern Plains and approaches the area Sunday 
morning. The general theme for much of these events where cold air 
has attempted to wrap in on the back side thus far this winter has 
been for the cold air to be late to arrive. As 850 mb temperatures 
approach -6C on the backside of the precip shield, the tendency for 
the precip shield later Sunday will be to dry out. It'll be a race 
against time though that maybe there could be a finish with snow on 
its back end after sunset Sunday. As cold air continues to push
in and the column dries out, an area of increased gradient 
keeps winds excited overnight and this will allow for the 
potential for gusts between 25 and 35 mph. 

As mentioned above, strong drying within subsidence occurs on the 
backside of the departing trough as high pressure to our south make 
its presence felt and mid level heights rise. Low level temperatures 
also warm back above freezing. It's interesting to see the GFS lag 
behind the other models including its AI counterpart for the mid 
week trough approaching from the southwest. There's still enough 
differences in these models to indicate that certainty is low on 
whether we get rain to end the end of next week. Between the NBM and 
a blend of the long range ensembles and operational guidance, there 
seems to be some agreement that the Thursday night into Friday 
morning time period presents the best chance to see rain. The GFS 
still lags this and sees the best chance waiting until Friday 
night/Saturday. It'll also be a breezy time period with 25 to 35 mph 
gusts possible. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 1124 AM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

Primarily IFR to low MVFR conditions will persist in occasional
light rain this afternoon. Improvement to VFR/dry remain on
track then for late this afternoon at KSBN, and early this 
evening at KFWA, as deeper moisture on the backside of a low 
pressure system exits east. Northwest to north winds near 10 
knots back to the west-southwest otherwise into tonight and 
Saturday.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 4 AM EST Saturday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Roller
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.text:
SPC AC 271600

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1000 AM CST Fri Nov 27 2026

   Valid 271630Z - 281200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the contiguous United
   States through tonight.

   ...Synopsis and Discussion...
   A mature mid/upper-level cyclone will move from the Mid-Atlantic to
   the Northeast today, with offshore low-level flow trajectories
   maintaining dry and/or stable conditions over much of the
   central/eastern CONUS. Overall thunderstorm potential will remain
   minimal, with a possible exception across parts of western OR. Here,
   weak MUCAPE and cool mid-level temperatures may support low-topped
   convection later this afternoon/evening beneath an eastward-moving
   mid/upper-level trough and associated strong westerly jet. While
   there is still some uncertainty with how much lightning will occur
   with this activity given the shallow depth of the weakly unstable
   layer, the chance for thunderstorms may be around 10%.

   ..Gleason/Karstens.. 11/27/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 271710

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1110 AM CST Fri Nov 27 2026

   Valid 281200Z - 291200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorm potential appears low on Saturday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough will amplify into the Plains on Saturday as a strong
   mid/upper speed max dives southeastward out of the Rockies.
   Substantial cooling aloft will spread across the Central Plains and
   across the Ozarks overnight and into Sunday morning, with
   strengthening wind fields including 50+ kt southwesterlies at 850
   mb.

   At the surface, low pressure is forecast to move from the Red River
   at 00Z to northern AR/southern MO through 12Z Sunday. Increasing
   southerly low-level winds will also bring dewpoints at or above 60 F
   as far north as southern AR, with 50s F dewpoints into southeast MO.

   Despite the otherwise favorable wind fields, instability will be
   weak, which when combined with overnight/early day timing, should
   support little if any severe storm risk through 12Z Sunday. However,
   increasing large-scale lift and moistening will support rain and a
   few elevated thunderstorms overnight.

   ..Jewell.. 11/27/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 271920

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0120 PM CST Fri Nov 27 2026

   Valid 291200Z - 301200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
   NORTHERN MISSISSIPPI...ALABAMA...AND SOUTHERN TENNESSEE...

   ...SUMMARY...
   At least isolated severe wind potential may develop into parts of
   northern Mississippi and Alabama Sunday.

   ...Discussion...
   A powerful upper trough will deepen as it moves east across the
   Mid/Lower MS Valley and toward the OH/TN Valleys later in the day.
   Substantial height falls and strengthening wind speeds will exist
   with this progressive trough which will reach the East Coast by 12Z
   Monday.

   A surface low will move northeastward and roughly along the OH River
   during the day, with a prominent cold front sweeping across KY, TN,
   MS and AL. Dewpoints in the 50s will develop as far north as KY,
   with 60+ over MS and AL.

   Given the antecedent dry air mass, the surface air mass will remain
   quite cool/saturated over much of the warm sector. SBCAPE is
   forecast to only reach a few hundred J/kg ahead of the cold front,
   which will provide the sole focus for storm potential.

   Initially isolated to scattered elevated storms are possible near
   the MS River early on Sunday, with gradually increasing coverage and
   consolidation along the cold front from Middle TN into eastern MS
   perhaps by midday, then into northern GA, eastern TN and KY by 00Z.

   The expected strongly forced line of low-topped convection should
   aid wind gust potential, as 50+ kt winds will exist just off the
   surface. A low-end risk of a tornado cannot be ruled out in a
   conditional sense, perhaps if pockets of heating or greater
   destabilization does develop. At this time, it appears a few severe
   gusts are most probable.

   ..Jewell.. 11/27/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
